clue.text: That chap, youngster, accompanying a legendary queen

parts.note: a man already mentioned is referred to as he
a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout

explanation.surface: A man and a child are escorting a queen from old stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecuba was queen of Troy in Greek legend, wife of Priam and mother of Hector.

clue.text: Australian city requires sound of laughter cut by half on part of The Simpsons

indicators.note: only the front half of the laughing noise is kept, the rest is cut away

parts.note: a hearty laugh is written ho ho
Bart is one of the family in the cartoon The Simpsons

explanation.surface: A city's tourist plan seems to need a halved laugh and a cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by half' keeps HO of HOHO; 'on' sets the cartoon son next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the state capital of Tasmania, an Australian city.

clue.text: Accountant's balance is variable in vehicle, former make

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the variable letter sits inside the pair of car words, between them

parts.note: Rover is a defunct British car make
in algebra y is a standard variable

explanation.surface: An accountant notes that a balance shifts depending on whether the car was a vintage make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like it points into the vehicle alone, but the variable sits between the two vehicle words; Rover was a British car maker that ceased production in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum brought forward from one account period to the next is what accountants call this.

clue.text: Merseyside town good for pirate

parts.note: Bootle is a town just north of Liverpool on Merseyside

explanation.surface: A northern town is presented as a fine place for a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOTLE is a town in Merseyside, the county around Liverpool in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective or verb, a pirated copy is an illicit, unlicensed one, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Did turn in vehicle traversing ice

indicators.note: the word for turn is placed inside the word for the snow vehicle

parts.note: a sled runs over ice and snow
to wind is to turn, as with a key or crank

explanation.surface: Someone performed a turn while riding a vehicle across ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'did' means cheated, as in 'I was done out of my money'.

clue.text: The appropriate way to fasten 11?

parts.note: 11 across is royalties, read as royal ties; the knot fit for royal neckwear is the one named after the royal house

explanation.surface: A question about how best to tie the item in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 11 as 'royal ties', the fitting knot carries the name of the British royal family's house.
explanation.definitionFit: This broad triangular necktie knot is named after the Duke of Windsor, a member of the royal house.

clue.text: Vehicle in rain crashed — fine state

indicators.note: the vehicle sits within the rearranged weather word
something crashed is wrecked, so the letters of rain are broken up

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van crashes in the rain, though someone insists everything is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' scrambles the weather word, and 'in' sets the vehicle inside it; 'fine' looks like weather talk but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism the term names a blissful condition of release, so loosely any perfect state.

clue.text: One's beset by fat landowner

indicators.note: the one is surrounded by the fat, which closes in on all sides

parts.note: lard is pig fat
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone is surrounded by an overweight owner of land.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a large estate is called by this title.

clue.text: Dilapidated old rum shop stocks poor spirits

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within it as a shop stocks goods

explanation.surface: A rundown shop selling old rum leaves its customers glum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dilapidated' and 'spirits' tempt toward an anagram or drink, but the run of letters spans dilapidateD OLD RUM Shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dumps, or low in mood, is a common figurative sense of this word.

clue.text: Grave argument in pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A serious quarrel breaks out in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient burial mound of earth is called by this name in archaeology.

clue.text: Sustaining motion in meeting I later disrupted

indicators.note: disrupted letters are thrown out of order and so need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting promises to disrupt it later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges only 'I later'; the leading 'in' is taken as written, with 'meeting' joining it on.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics, inertia is a body's tendency to keep moving, so this adjective describes keeping motion going.

clue.text: Author's income from connections in high places

definitions.meaning: writers earn a share of each sale of their books

explanation.definitionFit: Payments to writers per copy sold carry this name, and split as royal ties it means links with kings and queens.

clue.text: See TV heroine go wild with it

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Watch a television heroine go crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fashionable and in tune, or performing smoothly, just as being trendy does.

clue.text: Snake found in summer apparently

definitions.meaning: a viper, Britain's only venomous snake
read as sum-mer, one who does sums

explanation.surface: A snake turns up in the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apparently' flags that 'summer' is not the season but someone who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who totals figures is jokingly a summer, as is this word; it also names the viper.

clue.text: Saving meatier cooking — or rejecting it

indicators.note: cooking alters raw ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook could save a meaty dish, or simply refuse to eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: The diet that refuses meat, the 'it' of the clue, is exactly this way of life.

clue.text: Fancied one girl drinking a short

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the girl takes the drink in, so it goes inside her name

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name
a short is a small measure of spirits, such as gin

explanation.surface: A girl downs a quick spirit, and someone fancies her.
explanation.walkthrough: A short is a spirit served in a small measure, as opposed to a long drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fancied in the sense of dreamt up is unreal, a product of fantasy.

clue.text: Good times, good marks? Get away!

parts.note: ups, as in ups and downs
a teacher's tick marks a right answer

explanation.surface: Someone hearing of good times and good grades responds in disbelief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get away!' looks like the exclamation of disbelief, but here it is a plain instruction to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means to pack up and move home, so to go somewhere else.

clue.text: Soldier with 'chute heading for Hungary in airplane adjusted equipment

parts.note: a para is a parachute regiment soldier

indicators.note: adjusted letters are moved around into a different arrangement
the head of the country name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A paratrooper flies to Hungary and adjusts gear in the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges H plus AIRPLANE into PHERNALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an assortment of gear or accessories needed for some activity.

clue.text: Helping Shakespearean heroine cut down working

indicators.note: the name is trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: Portia is the heroine of The Merchant of Venice
on means functioning, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare heroine is being cut down to size while busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' removes the last A of PORTIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a serving of food, and a share like that is also called by this word.

clue.text: Ran like winds, having longer legs?

indicators.note: something that winds twists about, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A runner sped like the wind, perhaps because of their longer legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' seems to link 'Ran' and 'winds' but is part of the fodder, while 'winds' is the verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tall and thin with long limbs is described this way, so more so means more leggy.

clue.text: Son in marriage agreement

indicators.note: the son letter is set inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A son is part of his parents' marriage settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting together in harmony, in accord, is what this word means.

clue.text: Potato, say King Edward, put on ship

indicators.note: the king's letters are attached on the end of the vessel

parts.note: a tub is a slang word for a slow or clumsy ship
ER is Edwardus Rex, the royal cipher of King Edward

explanation.surface: A potato such as a King Edward is loaded onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a famous British potato variety, but here it is Edward Rex, ER. 'say' marks potato as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen underground stem that stores food, as a potato does, is botanically this.

clue.text: Watery lake in Paddington perhaps

indicators.note: the lake letter goes inside the animal

parts.note: Paddington is a famous storybook bear

explanation.surface: A lake turns up at Paddington, the London station, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is a London railway station but also the children's-book bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are dim and moist with tears are described by this old adjective.

clue.text: Being disturbed, enter into custody

indicators.note: letters that are disturbed are knocked out of place and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rowdy person who enters is taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention, keeping someone held, is one sense of this word.

clue.text: Kudos attached to Devon town

parts.note: kudos is praise or credit
on can mean fixed to, as a lid that is on

explanation.surface: A Devon town is credited with some prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Crediton is a market town in mid Devon, the county in south-west England.

clue.text: Tests a learner wearing swimming aids

indicators.note: the learner is put inside the fins, as a body is inside its gear

parts.note: flippers or fins help a swimmer
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A beginner wears flippers for swimming tests.
explanation.definitionFit: End-of-course university examinations are called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Bolt maybe second office machine needed

parts.note: a printer is a standard piece of office kit

explanation.surface: A bolt might need a second office machine to fix it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests a fastener; it is Usain Bolt, the champion runner, with 'maybe' marking an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt, the Olympic 100m champion, is a famous example of a fast short-distance runner.

clue.text: Carbon fibre that's used for colouring

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
rayon is a synthetic fibre

explanation.surface: A carbon fibre is described as something employed in dyeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A stick of coloured wax children draw with is what this word names.
